variants.asks: how much of the time are two charges opposed, in this theory?

probes.asks: the vacuum splits a point into two halves facing each other across an edge. What does this theory's meeting rule leave of them?
probes.found: ANNIHILATION leaves something behind in 0 of the 1 states a facing pair can be in - neutral meets neutral: both gone

measured.name: cases
measured.note: every combination the two ends can be carrying in G - no sign to carry, so one. Enumerated, not sampled

measured.name: surviving
measured.note: applying ANNIHILATION to each: neutral meets neutral: both gone

measured.name: annihilating
measured.note: the states in which ANNIHILATION left nothing at all: 1 of 1

steps.because: two charges are opposed exactly when their meeting leaves nothing - that is what the word means for a rule that either annihilates a pair or does not. The states a pair can be in are equally available, so how much of the time they are opposed is how many of those states annihilate, over how many there are
and left nothing at all in the other 1: those are the states in which the two were opposed, which is what being opposed MEANS in a theory whose meetings either annihilate a pair or do not

measured.name: surviving
measured.note: applying ANNIHILATION to each: neutral meets neutral: both gone

steps.because: a ray of G can be carrying nothing but itself, so a facing pair has 1 possible states and the enumeration is complete

measured.name: cases

steps.because: annihilating is 1 and cases is 1, both counted off the tiling, so the ratio is 1 exactly - and it is worth reading as annihilating/cases rather than as the number, because on another lattice it is a different number and the same ratio
